title: The handover, struck through
summary: The page splits in two: Kelwin's dark side on the left, your paper side on the right. Six draft documents cross the line between them one at a time, turn solid as they become yours, and strike out the six problems from the founder's letter, word for word.
story: This is the payoff. The six problems the letter listed in its margin are struck out, in the same order and words, as the asset that ends each one changes hands. It closes on you holding documents, which lets the next section, the method, show where the work starts.
motion: Standalone (plays on its own, done by about 5.9s): the heading rises as on every section. Kelwin's side explains itself on the heading's first line: its label, the word Handover set against the edge between the two sides, and the key (dashed = Drafted by Kelwin, solid = Owned by you) appear within the first quarter-second, before anything moves. The six dashed drafts settle into a stack on Kelwin's side, and the tray's headings and the six asset names fade in, each with its problem line still unstruck and a dotted empty place where its sheet will land.

Then the deal, one asset at a time, 01 to 06, a new one every 0.46s. Each sheet slides off the stack along a clear lane under the tray, crosses the line, and rises or drops into its place beside its asset. The sheet's edge turns from dashed to solid, and from light-on-dark to ink-on-paper, at the exact moment each part of it crosses the line. As it lands, its problem line is struck through by a drawn hairline (0.3s) and the new line rises in beneath it.

No sheet ever passes over text, a label or another sheet. Row-1 sheets rise through their partner's slot, which is still empty at that point. After the sixth lands, 'Yours · 06 of 06' appears in the title block, and a dashed outline is all that's left on Kelwin's side.

On the homepage, the heading and the waiting stack arrive when the section scrolls in. The deal starts once the lane the sheets travel along is fully on screen, so no sheet crosses out of sight. It plays once and nothing loops.

Hovering an asset lifts its sheet 8px and darkens its edge. With reduced motion, on phones, or if the animation library can't load, the finished state shows at once: every sheet handed over, every problem struck. Even with scripts off, the six problems still render struck (a plain hairline stands in for the drawn strike).
addressed: Your note on round 2's fit section ("I don't understand the point of having that animated line on the left side… confusing") applied here before you had to say it: Kelwin's dark side now explains itself on the first screen. The key (dashed = Drafted by Kelwin, solid = Owned by you) sits directly under the "Kelwin's side" label, and the edge between the two sides is labelled Handover on the same line as the section's own label, so it reads left to right as Kelwin's side, Handover, What you own, before a single sheet has moved and after they have all crossed.

Your recurring note, that every section repeats one layout (heading, figure panel, caption strip, toggle): this one has no panel, caption strip or toggle. The page itself splits into Kelwin's side and yours, and the edge between them is the handover line.

'Animations must be creative, authoritative and understandable at first glance, never an afterthought': each asset gets one clear move. A dashed draft leaves Kelwin's stack, turns solid as it crosses onto your side, lands next to its name, and the problem it ends is struck out.
The story setup pays off. The six struck lines are the letter's margin lines, word for word and numbered 01 to 06 the same way, so a reader who saw them in the letter sees them crossed out here.

What you approved in round 2 is kept: the six document sheets, the three capability groups, the tags, the handover line with its one red tick, and the dashed/solid key from 'The handover, spread'; the six before-and-after shifts and 'Same team, same market' from 'The Switch Plate'. They are now one section, so each shift has a cause.
Two FAQ answers now sit here instead of in a list: 'documented so they survive team changes' is in the opening paragraph, and the handover test is the side note.
The word 'compound' stays at two uses on the page: the sixth new line reads 'Each quarter deposits into the next', from your About page.
notes: Built from the generator scratchpad/redesign/work/handover/gen.mjs: edit it and re-run rather than editing S.html by hand. Each sheet is drawn twice in its own slot, a draft copy (data-surface dark: dashed, paper strokes, graphite fill) and an owned copy (solid, ink on paper). During the deal, S.js translates the sheet from the stack and clips the two copies at the surface edge every frame, so the dashed-to-solid change happens exactly on the line. At rest the draft copy is clipped away in CSS, so the default CSS is the final state. Positions are measured with offsetLeft/offsetTop chains, which ignore transforms and the homepage zoom. Strikes are SVG lines built in JS, one per rendered line (Narrative OS's before wraps to two lines at the 228px text column). A ResizeObserver rebuilds them when the text re-wraps, for example on a skin change. GSAP drives the timeline. JS adds .is-ink once the SVG strikes exist; before that (or with scripts off) a 1px line-through in CSS keeps the default render the struck final state. Without it, or under reduced motion or at 760px or narrower, KM.init only draws the strikes. Deviations from STORY §3 (07): the deal stagger, the lane and the live trigger are changed for legibility; the tag sits under the name rather than under the sheet; the height is about 1,296px rather than about 1,100–1,200; the title block's last cell uses the end-cap wording 'Yours · 06 of 06'; the 8px tick runs across the edge rather than along it. 'Kelwin's side' is a caps label without the red square, so the section keeps a single label square in its label row. Focus lifting works through :focus-within; the asset items are not links in the mockup, so no extra tab stops were added. Mobile (760px or narrower): a graphite strip on top (label, key, then the footprint and the way across), the datum horizontal along its foot with the tick, then the head and a one-column tray, with no deal. Copy sources: assets X (names, tags, grouping, legend, datum), beforeafter X (befores and afters, 'Same team, same market'), FAQ X Q04 and Q05, and FirmAbout.tsx ('Each quarter deposits into the next'). Round-3 coherence pass: the line key moved from the foot of Kelwin's side to directly under its label, and the datum's label Handover moved from the lane to the top of the edge, on the head's label row, with a 10px leader touching the edge (one label for the datum; the red tick stays where the lane crosses). No new words. The stack and the lane deliberately stay low, under the tray: the deal only starts once the lane is fully on screen, and a stack moved up into the heading's screen would be out of view by then, so the sheets would fall in from off-screen. Mobile: the strip now reads label, key, Handover, then the lane with its tick.
